summary: NSP-Minnesota, a wholly owned Xcel Energy subsidiary, filed an 8-K on October 9, 2026 disclosing a Form 8.01 submission of an Electric Customer Rate Stability Plan with the Minnesota Public Utilities Commission as an alternative to a planned 2027 rate case. The plan proposes freezing customer base rates for calendar 2027 and 2028 while accelerating recognition of federal Investment Tax Credit benefits from five battery storage projects over two years, offsetting incremental revenue requirements from capital improvements, and continuing existing true-up and tracker mechanisms. An MPUC decision is requested by January 2027; absent approval, NSP expects to file an electric rate case in early 2027. This is a routine regulatory rate matter, not a special situation; no deal terms or arbitrage angle apply, with outcomes hinging on MPUC approval timing and the ITC acceleration accounting treatment.
